already adverb

also so soon, by now, for a long time already, for a long time now, long since

classical

Plaut. Men. 2.3.86: jamne ībis?, are you going so soon? (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 52: obsolēvit jam ista ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 270
Traupman 285

jam

adverb

already, by now

Jamne …? asks “already?”. With a negative, “no longer”: jam nōn, nōn jam; “not yet” is nōndum (see not yet).

Other words

  • jam dūdum (jam diū) — for a long time already (with a present tense)

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 816: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.; Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; Traupman 88: I’ve been here a long time already, jam dūdum adsum; Traupman 285

    Latin keeps the present where English says “have been”: jam dūdum adsum, I’ve been here for ages (Traupman 88).

Examples

  • Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    My mind’s been on the dishes for ages.Ter. Eun. 816

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    I haven’t known how you are for a long time now; you don’t writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1

See also not yet, now, it’s getting dark.
